methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous systematic review with PRISMA protocol registered (PROSPERO CRD420251062013). Comprehensive FDA database search (1 Jan 2009 - 31 Dec 2024) with two-stage independent study selection by paired reviewers. Risk-of-bias assessment using RoB2 tool on all 36 trials; low bias across all included studies. Random-effects meta-regression using inverse-variance method with restricted maximum likelihood variance estimation. Subgroup analyses stratified by tumor type and drug class. Sensitivity analysis with arcsine-transformed proportions. Collinearity assessment documented (VIF reported).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Systematic review of RCTs (LoE: 2a per Oxford CEBM). Addresses clinically important question: whether ECOG PS2 patients derive comparable benefit from anticancer therapies. Finds no significant difference in efficacy (PFS HR 0.45 [PS2] vs 0.52 [PS≤1], OS HR 0.81 vs 0.71), supporting broader trial eligibility. However, greater toxicity risk (SAEs, treatment discontinuations, AE-related deaths) with higher PS2 representation. Practical relevance: informs trial design and patient selection. Limited novelty: prior meta-analyses (2017-2020) addressed similar questions; authors acknowledge previous work but claim first to analyze PS2 separately.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive PRISMA adherence: PRISMA 2020 checklist in supplementary; flow diagram (Supplementary Figure S1); detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria explicitly stated; dual independent study selection documented with consensus method for disagreements. Data extraction tables (Supplementary Tables S4-S6) present study characteristics, PS distribution (median 49.4% PS0, 44.3% PS1, 4.1% PS2), and outcome HRs. Meta-regression models with β coefficients and 95% CIs reported. Limitations acknowledged. Gaps: some supplementary figures/tables referenced as 'REDACTED'; funnel plots reported but Egger's test availability unclear; no protocol available online.

novelty_literature.justification: Addresses documented gap: first to systematically analyze PS2 participants separately (prior meta-analyses 2017-2020 grouped PS1+PS2). Extends prior work by Cheng et al. (2017), checkpoint inhibitor meta-analyses (2018, 2020). Finding (no efficacy difference) somewhat expected given known PS1 data; novelty is in granular PS2 analysis. Contributes practical knowledge for trial design regarding PS2 inclusion rationale. However, conclusion (PS2 should be included) is not paradigm-shifting; reinforces known principle that performance status heterogeneity should inform trial design.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear progression: problem statement (PS2 exclusion limits generalizability), methods (36 trials, FDA-based search), results (no efficacy difference, increased toxicity), discussion (implications for trial design). Forest plots (Figures 1-2) effectively display hazard ratios with confidence intervals across performance strata. Tables 1-3 comprehensively present meta-regression coefficients with P values and 95% CIs. Discussion thoughtfully addresses ecological fallacy limitation, selection bias of trial-enrolled PS2 patients versus real-world populations. Minor: dense discussion section with multiple citations.

key_strengths: Rigorous methodology: PRISMA-registered protocol, RoB2 assessment showing low bias across 36 FDA-approved trials, random-effects meta-regression with sensitivity analyses using arcsine-transformed proportions for robustness

First systematic analysis of PS2 participants separately: meta-regression shows no significant efficacy difference (PFS HR 0.45 [PS2] vs 0.52 [PS≤1], P=0.59; OS HR 0.81 vs 0.71, P=0.18) versus prior studies grouping PS1+PS2

Comprehensive safety profiling: higher PS2 representation significantly associated with SAEs, treatment discontinuations, and AE-related deaths (β=0.0609, P=0.0093 for SAEs), quantifying vulnerability of this population
Practical implications: supports wider PS2 enrollment in cancer trials to improve generalizability and reflect real-world patient populations encountered in clinical practice
key_concerns: Limited novelty: finding (no PS2 efficacy difference) somewhat expected given prior PS1 data; conclusion supports inclusion of PS2 but represents incremental rather than paradigm-shifting knowledge contribution

Selection bias acknowledged but incompletely addressed: PS2 patients in trials are highly selected (controlled comorbidities), likely fitter than real-world PS2 population; findings may overestimate efficacy and underestimate toxicity in routine practice
Ecological fallacy risk: using study-level aggregated PS proportions to model individual-level treatment benefit; authors acknowledge but note consistency between subgroup and meta-regression results

Small PS2 representation limits statistical power: median only 4.1% of trial participants were PS2; only 16 trials reported PS2-specific outcomes; multivariable meta-regression models often non-significant for PS2 coefficients (due to small sample size and collinearity with PS1)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: rigorous systematic review with comprehensive methodology addressing clinically relevant question of PS2 inclusion in pivotal trials. Findings support broader enrollment for generalizability. Limitations appropriately disclosed. Recommend minor revisions clarifying selection bias implications and explicitly discussing gap between trial-enrolled vs real-world PS2 populations before acceptance at Tier 3.
